tasks.title: Rewrite ralph init with interactive property-by-property flow
tasks.description:
Rewrite the ralph.json scaffolding section of lib/ralph_init.sh as an npm init-style interactive prompt flow. Each property shows its current/default value in brackets; pressing Enter accepts the default.

Prompt flow (in order):
```
Project name [<basename of project root>]:
Description (used in agent system prompts) []:
Health check command (auto-detected if blank) []:
Default test command []:
Implementation file [IMPLEMENTATION.md]:
Truncate agent text output? [Y/n]:
CLAUDE.md glob pattern for summarize []:
Enable TTS narration? [y/N]:
Narration voice [bf_emma]:              # only if narration enabled
ntfy push notification topic []:         # only if narration enabled
```

Re-init support: When ralph.json already exists, parse it first with Python (similar to how ralph_config.sh does it) and use the current values as bracket defaults instead of the hardcoded defaults. This makes re-init a way to update config interactively.

For the truncateText prompt, convert Y/n input to a boolean true/false in the JSON. Default is true (Y).

After collecting all values, write ralph.json with the collected values using a Python heredoc for proper JSON formatting (avoid shell string escaping issues).

Preserve the existing narration hooks installation logic that runs after config writing (lines 82-171 of current file). Also preserve the .ralph/ directory creation and tasks.json creation at the top.

Update the 'Next steps' message at the end — remove the 'Edit ralph.json' step since init now covers all fields.
tasks.notes: Rewrote ralph_init.sh with npm init-style interactive prompts for all ralph.json properties. Re-init parses existing config via Python for bracket defaults. JSON written via Python heredoc with all values passed as argv for safe escaping. Narration voice/ntfy prompts only shown when narration is enabled. Boolean Y/n prompts properly convert to JSON true/false. Narration hooks logic preserved unchanged. Next steps message simplified.

tasks.title: Add instructions.md creation offer to ralph init
tasks.description:
After writing ralph.json in lib/ralph_init.sh, add a prompt offering to create .ralph/instructions.md:

```
Create .ralph/instructions.md for personal agent preferences? [y/N]
```

If the user answers yes:
1. Create .ralph/instructions.md as an empty file (touch it)
2. Open it with $EDITOR (fall back to vi if EDITOR is unset): ${EDITOR:-vi} "$RALPH_DATA_DIR/instructions.md"

Also update .ralph/.gitignore to include instructions.md:
- For new projects (gitignore just created by init): add `instructions.md` to the initial cat heredoc
- For existing projects (gitignore already exists): append `instructions.md` if not already present. Use a grep check: `grep -qxF 'instructions.md' "$GITIGNORE" || echo 'instructions.md' >> "$GITIGNORE"`

This should go after the ralph.json writing block but before the narration hooks section.

tasks.title: Inject instructions.md into execution agent system prompts
tasks.description:
In lib/ralph_execute.sh, modify build_system_prompt() to inject .ralph/instructions.md contents into the system prompt for execution agents.

After the project_desc block (around line 159), add:

```bash
local personal_instructions=""
local instructions_file="$RALPH_DATA_DIR/instructions.md"
if [[ -f "$instructions_file" ]] && [[ -s "$instructions_file" ]]; then
    personal_instructions=$(cat "$instructions_file")
fi
```

Then in the cat <<SYSPROMPT heredoc (starts around line 188), after the project description line, inject:

```
$(if [[ -n "$personal_instructions" ]]; then
echo "
PERSONAL INSTRUCTIONS:
$personal_instructions
"
fi)
```

IMPORTANT: Do NOT modify ralph_plan.sh. This is execution agents only — planning should stay neutral.

Note: RALPH_DATA_DIR is already available in this file (set earlier as the .ralph directory path).

tasks.description:
